picks.title: Interior with Young Woman Seen from Behind
picks.creator: Vilhelm Hammershøi
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Vilhelm Hammershøi, Interior with Young Woman Seen from Behind, 1903–04, Randers Kunstmuseum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A lone woman in black stands with her back to us on the right, facing a bare grey wall; the left half is almost empty wall, an ideal quiet field for the title. Borrow the muted grey palette, the turned-away figure (isolation without melodrama) and the generous negative space.

picks.title: The Monk by the Sea
picks.creator: Caspar David Friedrich
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Caspar David Friedrich, The Monk by the Sea, 1808–10, Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: One tiny figure against an enormous empty sky and dark sea: the classic image of smallness and solitude. About four-fifths of the canvas is sky, so a title fits in the upper left; the low horizon and desaturated tones carry exhaustion quietly.

picks.title: Silhouette eines Steinwälzers
picks.creator: Stephan Sprinz
picks.credit: "Silhouette eines Steinwälzers" by Stephan Sprinz, CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0), via Wikimedia Commons
picks.why: A single small bird (a turnstone) stands on a dark rock, right of centre, facing left into a wide, softly blurred dusk sky. The empty left half is ready-made space for the title, and the lone figure gazing into it gives the quiet, slightly lonely mood. Borrow the low dark base, the one small subject placed right of centre, and the defocused dusk gradient.

picks.title: Slovenian Sunset (7027587519)
picks.creator: whatleydude (from London, United Kingdom)
picks.credit: "Slovenian Sunset (7027587519)" by whatleydude from London, United Kingdom, CC BY 2.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0), via Wikimedia Commons
picks.why: One tiny rowing boat sits low in a vast, even expanse of sea and sky, so the empty space carries the feeling of isolation. The calm horizontal bands leave plenty of quiet room for type. For burnout, borrow the sense of scale (one small figure, a huge quiet field) and cool the warm sunset towards blues and greys.

Y.note: Put the title in the open sky on the left; with the boat image, crop so the boat sits in the right third.

picks.title: A Village Choir
picks.creator: Thomas Webster
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Thomas Webster, A Village Choir, 1847, Victoria and Albert Museum, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A crowded church gallery of ordinary villagers singing and playing together, in a warm brown and amber palette. It shows exactly the community-choir-in-a-church idea; borrow the packed, overlapping faces and the warm candle-wood tones for a poster that feels homely, not formal.

picks.title: Watoto Church Choir singing during the 33rd Coronation anniversary
picks.creator: Namwanje Sauyah
picks.credit: Photo: Namwanje Sauyah, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A dense row of singers in bright, warm clothing, mouths open mid-song, with faces repeating into the depth of the frame: 'lots of voices together' made visible. It is a church choir but photographed at a civic event, not inside a church, so use it for the crowd rhythm and warmth. Identifiable people: CC0 covers copyright, not personality rights, so check before using it in advertising.

picks.title: The Organ Rehearsal
picks.creator: Henry Lerolle
picks.licence: CC0 (Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access)
picks.credit: Henry Lerolle, The Organ Rehearsal, 1885. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. CC0.
picks.why: A singer and listeners in a church choir loft beside the organ pipes, lit by soft, warm light from the windows: exactly the setting of a choir concert in a church. Borrow the warm, hushed light, the organ as a backdrop, and the feeling of people gathered around music.

picks.title: Watoto Church Choir singing during the 33rd Coronation anniversary
picks.creator: Namwanje Sauyah
picks.credit: Namwanje Sauyah, Watoto Church Choir singing, 2026, via Wikimedia Commons (CC0).
picks.why: A full choir performing together: many voices massed as one group, which is the 'lots of voices together' part of the brief. Borrow the packed group, the repetition of faces and robes, and the sense of a shared performance.

Y.note: These two came from a web search; the reference collection had church interiors but no choirs. The choir photo shows identifiable people: copyright is waived (CC0), but in promotional use their personality rights may still apply, so a crop or a local choir's own photo is safer.

picks.title: Seeing stars (SEST telescope at La Silla)
picks.creator: Sangku Kim / ESO
picks.credit: Sangku Kim/ESO, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A big dish stands alone under a dark star field, attentive and still. It reads as 'listening and watching' without screens, code or hoodies. Borrow the dark-blue night, the single sensor turned toward the unknown, and the tension of a small lit structure against vast darkness.

picks.title: The IRAM 30-meter telescope scanning the night sky
picks.creator: IRAM-gre (IRAM)
picks.credit: IRAM-gre, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A radio telescope sweeping the night sky: constant, active vigilance, which is the idea behind security monitoring. Its strong geometric silhouette crops well for a wide hero. Note: CC BY-SA means a modified version (a crop or overlay) must be shared under the same licence, so check that suits the website.

picks.title: Everywhere Eyeballs are Aflame
picks.creator: Odilon Redon
picks.licence: CC0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
picks.credit: Odilon Redon, Everywhere Eyeballs are Aflame, 1888. Cleveland Museum of Art. CC0.
picks.why: A single detached eye hangs in a pale opening above dark rocks: watchfulness turned into one uncanny image, with strong light–dark tension. It says 'we are watching' without any hacker-hoodie cliché. Borrow the lone eye or sensor motif in a small bright opening inside a mostly black field.

picks.title: Backlit laptop keyboard (Unsplash)
picks.creator: Markus Petritz (petritzdesigns)
picks.credit: "Backlit laptop keyboard (Unsplash)" by Markus Petritz, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
picks.why: A tight, low view of a backlit keyboard: one narrow band of keys is sharp and the rows around it blur into darkness and screen glow. It reads as technology at night, focused and a little tense, with no people. Borrow the shallow focus band and the dark, glowing palette as a quiet background for the hero copy.

picks.title: Fishermen on beach harvesting salmon catch, vicinity of the lower Columbia River, ca 1900
picks.creator: John Fletcher Ford
picks.licence: Public domain (per Wikimedia Commons; University of Washington Industries and Occupations Photographs Collection)
picks.credit: John Fletcher Ford, Fishermen on beach harvesting salmon catch, lower Columbia River, ca. 1900. University of Washington Libraries, Special Collections, via Wikimedia Commons (public domain).
picks.why: A historical record of a seine haul heaped with salmon: the 'past' abundance in one frame. Set against a single fish or a near-empty field, it makes the decline visible through scale contrast. Borrow the dense mass of fish as the 'then' half of a then-and-now cover.

picks.title: Alaska salmon jumping out of water
picks.creator: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
picks.licence: Public domain (US federal government work, per Wikimedia Commons)
picks.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Alaska salmon jumping out of water, via Wikimedia Commons (public domain).
picks.why: One salmon alone in the air above the water: the 'now' half, with the fish isolated rather than massed. Paired with the crowded historical haul, or shrunk to a tiny subject in a large empty field, it shows how small the remaining population is. Borrow the single isolated fish surrounded by empty space.

X.note: Both picks came from a web search; the reference collection had scale-contrast and negative-space examples but no salmon. The 1900 photo has 'Copyrighted' written on the print, but as a US work published before 1931 it is public domain. The jumping-salmon file reached Commons through a third-party public-domain image site, so check the USFWS origin before print use.

picks.title: Fishermen on beach harvesting salmon catch, vicinity of the lower Columbia River, ca 1900
picks.creator: John Fletcher Ford
picks.date: c. 1900 (University of Washington Libraries, Industries and Occupations Photographs, INDOCC 631)
picks.credit: John Fletcher Ford, c. 1900. University of Washington Libraries Special Collections. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A beach covered in salmon from one seine haul shows historic abundance at a glance. Use it as the 'past' half of a then/now contrast, perhaps faded sepia, against a sparse present-day image. The print's 'Copyrighted' caption dates from c. 1900; that copyright has long expired.

picks.title: Sockeye salmon sun glistening
picks.creator: Lisa Hupp / U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
picks.date: undated (in USFWS 2021 Fish and Aquatic Conservation Annual Report)
picks.licence: Public domain (work of a US federal employee)
picks.credit: Lisa Hupp/USFWS. Public domain.
picks.why: A single red sockeye in clear water: the 'now' half, one fish where there were thousands. Put it small in a lot of empty space, or set it beside the 1900 haul, so the scale gap reads instantly on the cover. Not a US government endorsement; credit USFWS as courtesy.

picks.title: Domaći hljeb sa sjemenkama u pekari (home-style seeded bread in a bakery)
picks.creator: Minja Klarić
picks.credit: Minja Klarić, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: One dark, seed-crusted loaf stands upright in front of a rack of pale white loaves. It is almost exactly the brief: one loaf distinguished by texture and colour. The vertical framing suits a 4:5 or Story crop. CC BY-SA: edits must stay under CC BY-SA, with credit given.

picks.title: The Baker
picks.creator: Job Adriaensz. Berckheyde
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Job Berckheyde, The Baker, c. 1681, Worcester Art Museum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A Haarlem baker blows a horn to announce fresh bread, with loaves on the sill: heritage, craft and celebration together. It works as a mood and layout reference for an anniversary post: a window frame, warm light, and the bread presented like a proud announcement.

picks.title: Odd one out (6097084986)
picks.creator: ^ Missi ^ (from Mississauga, Canada)
picks.credit: "Odd one out (6097084986)" by ^ Missi ^ from Mississauga, Canada, CC BY 2.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0), via Wikimedia Commons
picks.why: A tight grid of identical red sneakers broken by one blue shoe turned the other way: the clearest model of 'one that stands out from all the others'. Borrow the composition: fill the square with rows of identical loaves and make one different in colour, glaze, shape or direction (a golden anniversary loaf, say).

picks.title: Loaves of Bread (Unsplash)
picks.creator: Clark Young
picks.credit: Clark Young, Loaves of Bread, 2016, via Wikimedia Commons / Unsplash (CC0).
picks.why: Rows of crusty loaves on a bakery shelf provide the repeated field the idea needs, with the warm palette and texture of real bread. Use it as the style and lighting reference for 'all the others', then light, colour or garnish the hero loaf so it breaks the pattern.

Y.note: The sneaker pick came from the reference collection; the bread photo came from a web search.

picks.title: Fantastic Landscape
picks.creator: Francesco Guardi
picks.licence: CC0 (Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access)
picks.credit: Francesco Guardi, Fantastic Landscape, ca. 1765. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1941. CC0.
picks.why: A long wall and quay recede from the left foreground through an arch towards a pale, open distance of water and hills. The receding lines carry the eye to the horizon, and the big sky leaves room for 'Where we are going'. Borrow the converging edges that lead to a bright, low horizon.

picks.title: Mist Rising at Sunset in the Catskills
picks.creator: Sanford Robinson Gifford
picks.credit: Sanford Robinson Gifford, Mist Rising at Sunset in the Catskills, c. 1861. Art Institute of Chicago. CC0.
picks.why: Glowing orange bands of cloud and light reflected on the water sit along the horizon above darker hills, so the brightest, warmest area is the far distance. On a divider slide, that pulls the eye outward and forward. Borrow the light gradient: dark foreground, luminous distance.

picks.title: The Avenue at Middelharnis
picks.creator: Meindert Hobbema
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Meindert Hobbema, The Avenue at Middelharnis, 1689, National Gallery, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: The textbook one-point perspective: a road lined with tall trees runs straight to a vanishing point on a low horizon, under a big sky. Borrow the converging lines that drag the eye forward, and put 'Where we are going' in the open sky.

picks.title: Historic Route 66 near Amboy, California
picks.creator: Dietmar Rabich
picks.credit: Dietmar Rabich / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0
picks.why: A straight desert road running to the horizon in a wide panoramic format (about 2:1), so it suits a 16:9 slide. A clean, modern take on the same pull-to-the-horizon idea. CC BY-SA: credit the author; adapted versions must carry the same licence.

picks.title: Moonlight, Wood Island Light
picks.creator: Winslow Homer
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: Winslow Homer, Moonlight, Wood Island Light, 1894, The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Public domain.
picks.why: A night sea crashing on rocks, nearly all dark, with a lighthouse's small point of light in the distance. It suits a literary cover: painterly, menacing, restrained. Borrow the near-black palette and the single distant light as the focal point.

picks.title: Sidi Bou Afi Lighthouse, El Jadida, Morocco
picks.creator: Belbachirkamal
picks.credit: Belbachirkamal, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A lighthouse at night in fog, its beams visible as solid shafts against a dark sky, in portrait orientation like a book cover. Borrow the beam as a graphic element, which can also point to the title. CC BY-SA: the cover design built on it may need to be licensed CC BY-SA, so a commercial publisher may prefer it as a reference only.

picks.title: Moonlight, Wood Island Light
picks.creator: Winslow Homer
picks.licence: Public domain (artwork held by The Metropolitan Museum of Art)
picks.credit: Winslow Homer, Moonlight, Wood Island Light, 1894. The Metropolitan Museum of Art.
picks.why: A night sea crashing on rocks, mostly in deep dark tones, with the small, distant lighthouse light as the focal point. It matches the setting and mood of a literary thriller. Borrow the near-black palette, the heavy surf and the single small light in the distance.

picks.title: He Raises the Bronze Urn
picks.creator: Odilon Redon
picks.licence: CC0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
picks.credit: Odilon Redon, He Raises the Bronze Urn, 1888. Cleveland Museum of Art. CC0.
picks.why: A dense black lithograph in which one intense burst of light, raised overhead, cuts through the darkness while a black diagonal mass swallows the right side. It is a strong model of 'mostly dark, one strong light' with mystery and unease. Borrow the single radiating light source and the deep velvety blacks for a portrait-format cover.

Y.note: The Homer came from a web search (the reference collection had no lighthouse); the Redon came from the reference collection.

picks.title: Branch of the Seine near Giverny (Mist)
picks.creator: Claude Monet
picks.credit: Claude Monet, Branch of the Seine near Giverny (Mist), 1897. Art Institute of Chicago. CC0.
picks.why: Muted blue, lavender and pale pink dissolve into each other in morning mist, with almost no hard edges or detail. It feels calm and soft, and nothing in it is busy. Borrow the limited cool palette and the soft transitions; the broad pale area on the right takes banner text easily.

picks.title: Mishima: Morning Mist, from the series Fifty-three Stations of the Tokaido Road (Hoeido Tokaido)
picks.creator: Utagawa Hiroshige
picks.credit: Utagawa Hiroshige, Mishima: Morning Mist, c. 1833/34. Art Institute of Chicago. CC0.
picks.why: Shapes fade into layers of grey mist behind the travellers, so the background turns silent and soft. Borrow the layered, fading silhouettes (soft grey planes receding) as a gentle, low-contrast backdrop for a sleep feature. Leave out the busier foreground figures.

picks.title: Nocturne: Blue and Silver – Chelsea
picks.creator: James McNeill Whistler
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: James McNeill Whistler, Nocturne: Blue and Silver – Chelsea, 1871, Tate. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: Almost a single field of soft blue-green with a low horizon, a few faint lights and one small boat. It is the calmest image I know, and easy to crop wide. Borrow the one-hue palette, the misty edges and the near-absence of detail for a sleep banner with text overlaid.

picks.title: Moonlight, Strandgade 30
picks.creator: Vilhelm Hammershøi
picks.licence: CC0 (The Met Open Access; public-domain painting)
picks.credit: Vilhelm Hammershøi, Moonlight, Strandgade 30, 1900–06, The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Open Access, CC0).
picks.why: An empty room at night, with soft moonlight from a window falling on the wall and floor. It feels hushed and domestic, like a bedroom just before sleep. Borrow the low-contrast greys, the single soft light source, and the absence of anything busy.

picks.title: Profile Portrait of the Printers Brunet and Lasteyrie
picks.creator: Dominique-Vivant Denon
picks.credit: Dominique-Vivant Denon, Profile Portrait of the Printers Brunet and Lasteyrie, 1816. Art Institute of Chicago. CC0.
picks.why: Two men in profile, of different size, age and drawing style, overlap slightly and face the same way. That is 'belong together but different' in one picture: two distinct identities with a shared direction. Borrow the overlapping pair facing one way as a metaphor for two departments with one heading.

picks.title: William Howard Taft Presidential Inaugural Medal
picks.creator: Joseph K. Davison's Sons
picks.credit: Joseph K. Davison's Sons, William Howard Taft Presidential Inaugural Medal, 1909. Smithsonian American Art Museum. CC0.
picks.why: Two faces of one gold medal shown side by side on black, portraits on one side and inscription on the other: two different faces of one object. Borrow the two-up layout on a dark ground, with shared material and colour showing unity while each side keeps its own content.

picks.title: Meeting of Waters (Manaus)
picks.creator: Ana Claudia Jatahy – MTUR (Brazilian Ministry of Tourism)
picks.licence: CC0 (as tagged on Commons, from the Ministry of Tourism Flickr)
picks.credit: Ana Claudia Jatahy / MTUR, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: The dark Rio Negro and the sandy Solimões run side by side as one river without mixing at first: two departments that are clearly different but now share one channel. Borrow the clean two-tone split for the slide, with each half labelled.

picks.title: Confluence de l'Arve et du Rhône (Geneva)
picks.creator: Christian David
picks.credit: Christian David, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: The clear blue Rhône meets the silty grey Arve and they flow on together, with a visible seam between them. It is a European, urban counterpart to the Manaus image, and the high-resolution landscape format suits a slide. Credit the author.

picks.title: Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway
picks.creator: J. M. W. Turner
picks.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons tag; author died 70+ years ago)
picks.credit: J. M. W. Turner, Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway, 1844, National Gallery, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A locomotive bursts out of golden haze along a diagonal bridge: the classic painting of energy and the new rushing forward. Borrow the strong diagonal, the warm, high-energy palette and the motion blur for a spread about growth, while keeping the reference abstract rather than literally Victorian.

picks.title: Night Light Trail, Maryland, Lagos, Nigeria
picks.creator: Omoeko Media
picks.credit: Omoeko Media, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
picks.why: A long exposure of traffic streaming through Lagos at night: literal forward motion in a fast-growing emerging-market city, which avoids generic stock skylines. Borrow the streaking light lines as a directional graphic motif across the spread. CC BY-SA: adaptations must stay under the same licence; I did not view this image myself.

picks.title: Frigate Bird Silhouette Against St Lucia Sunset 5738
picks.creator: ImagePerson
picks.credit: "Frigate Bird Silhouette Against St Lucia Sunset 5738" by ImagePerson, CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0), via Wikimedia Commons
picks.why: A bird with wings fully spread glides diagonally across warm, luminous clouds: crisp, confident, forward motion. On a spread, the diagonal wing line drives the eye across the page. Borrow the single dynamic silhouette on a bright, warm field, and the strong diagonal.

picks.title: Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway
picks.creator: J. M. W. Turner
picks.credit: J. M. W. Turner, Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway, 1844. National Gallery, London.
picks.why: A train rushes out of a golden haze towards the viewer along a hard diagonal bridge: a classic image of energy, progress and forward movement. Borrow the strong diagonal into depth, the blurred atmospheric speed and the warm, rising light, which suit a growth story without literal charts.

Y.note: The bird came from the reference collection; the Turner came from a web search.
